hands:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: transparent hand sprite atlas for the attached Goo character, to replace unnatural tiny procedural hands in an animated film.
Use the reference only to match the peach watercolor skin, dark brown ink outline and midcentury illustration technique. Draw SIX isolated HUMAN CARTOON HANDS, one in each cell of an evenly spaced three-column two-row grid. Transparent background, no text, no labels, no arms, no clothing, no objects. Each hand includes a short wrist, with the wrist at the bottom center of its cell and fingers generally above it. All six have the SAME adult hand size and same wrist thickness. The forearm axis is vertical. Keep each entirely within its cell with generous space.
These are the hands of a stocky friendly adult with soft rounded proportions. They must be anatomically convincing, with a broad substantial palm, a clearly opposed thumb, natural finger lengths, correct finger joints and organic asymmetry. Five fingers total including thumb, four fingers plus thumb. Fingers slightly tapered and bent, never petal-shaped or evenly spaced like sausages. No rubber glove, no animal paw, no baby hand, no skeletal realistic hand. Rounded knuckles; no harsh tiny crosshatching. Bold smooth dark brown contour, warm opaque peach and gentle paper grain inside.
Top row:
1. relaxed hanging hand, dorsal three-quarter view: four fingers softly bent together, thumb resting beside index; the hand is drawn upright with wrist below for rigging.
2. presenting open palm, palm three-quarter view: fingers loosely gathered and gently curled, thumb naturally separated to viewer-left, welcoming gesture, not a flat stop-sign or a splayed star.
3. pointing with index extended upward, remaining three fingers naturally curled into the palm, thumb resting across them. Index is softly bent, not perfectly rigid. Clear fingertip at top.
Bottom row:
4. relaxed supportive fist for resting chin: curled fingers viewed from the side, broad smooth knuckles across top, thumb alongside rather than clenched tightly.
5. head-scratching hand, fingers naturally curved toward an implied scalp above the hand; pads and bent fingers visible, no scalp or object drawn.
6. light precision grip for holding a pencil, thumb and index gently pinch an invisible thin pencil, middle finger supports it, remaining fingers curl loosely. No actual pencil.
All wrists clean and broad enough to attach under a hoodie cuff. Consistent lighting, color and rendering across all six; transparent outside the clean contours.
